title: Dodge's film of Bunk and his friendship with Bubber Miley
summary: Dodge as a ballet dancer, his silent movie of Bunk, and his friendship with Bubber Miley.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I knew him quite well. One thing I often think of now, he made a movie of Bunk one time at, probably in Washington Square. But somehow in my mind, it doesn't seem like Washington Square when I pictured. It might have been like Gramercy Square someplace else. It was a silent movie, unfortunately. And maybe only ran about five minutes or so. Out in the public park, just a bunk moving around.

Unfortunately, I never answered his last letter. I wish I had now. I have it someplace here. I owe hundreds of letters, actually. But he wrote me, oh, roughly 1958 or something along in there. And he was still in New York. I had written him a few off and on through the years. I would occasionally hear from him. He was reviewing records, but I hadn't heard anything about him or from him, of course. It's been, oh, 15 years or so now. He may not even be living, I don't know. But some of these days I'll try to find out. Because I would like to see him again. He wasn't that close a friend, but still I used to see him quite often in New York. He'd been a dancer, you know, for the Metropolitan Opera. And particularly, he particularly liked Bubber Miley. He was a big favorite of his and a friend, personal friend, too. And he had Bubber, I think, here at the Metropolitan Opera Ballet. And had Bubber to play a special solo on some ballet they did one time.
Bubber at this time would be playing in New York?
He'd been with Ellington, I think, at that period, probably. Right.
He didn't live that long. That must have been quite early.
Yeah, it would have to be in the 20s.

Did you know that Bubber Miley, speaking about Bubber Miley, played with some orchestra that was put together, even by Hoagy Carmichael in New York, when he was recording Big Spider-Beck in a, and I forgot the name of the song, it isn't Barnacle Bill the Sailor, but there's one there in which they have Bubber Miley and Big Spider-Beck playing two cornet solos, or one trumpet. I can't think of a greater contrast.
Yeah, I may faintly remember that. It doesn't hardly register in my mind. I think I didn't hear.
It was just amazing, the contrast and styles between the two of them.
So I don't even know how Roger Dodge made his living in those late years, not all he did.
